title: The Lord Is My Shepherd
summary: The Shepherd does all the work and goes before us. And the valley is only the shadow of death. A shadow can't bite.
exhortation: A couple of points from this beautiful psalm. First, the obvious one: the Lord, our Savior Jesus Christ, is our shepherd. That means he is with us every step of the way, and he is doing all the work. He knows where we're going and how to get there. He has scouted the best resting places and the best paths. When wolves come, he is the one who defeats them.

The second point I got from my pastor when he preached on Psalm 23: though we walk through the valley of the shadow of death, remember that it is only a shadow. Because of what Jesus did on the cross and because he rose from the dead, death is a defeated enemy. It is now just a shadow. The shadow of a fierce dog is frightening, but it can't bite you. The shadow of a knife can't cut you. And the shadow of death can't kill you. In fact, death can only bring us where we long to be: in the house of the Lord, with Jesus.

So as we walk through life today, there will be many shadows that terrify and distract us. Don't let them. Fix your eyes on Jesus. Keep your focus on the Shepherd who has gone before us and cleared the way so that we can pass through safely.
prayer: Lord, thank you for meeting us this morning. Thank you that your mercies are new every day.
We praise you, we honor you, and we thank you for your mercy and kindness toward us.
